citations.narrative:
During a review of the medical activity records, the inspector identified documentation referencing an injury involving a
Southern three banded armadillo. Further review determined that, on 06/29/2026, a keeper left the armadillo’s enclosure
‑
door unlocked, allowing the animal to fall approximately 3–4 feet to the ground. A member of the public witnessed the
incident and notified a nearby keeper, after which staff transported the armadillo for veterinary evaluation. The facility had
no additional records available for review regarding the incident at the time of inspection.
Even though the animal was found to be in good health in this case, lack of careful handling resulted in the animal’s fall
and created a risk of physical harm, trauma, behavioral stress, and unnecessary discomfort, which could adversely affect
the animal’s well being.
‑
Handling of all animals shall be done as expeditiously and carefully as possible in a manner that does not cause trauma,
behavioral stress, physical harm, or unnecessary discomfort.
Correct by: September 24, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture

Mailstop #3W11
